function.text: NTRK2 encodes the TRKB neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase, which regulates neuronal survival, differentiation, and function. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase involved in the development and the maturation of the central and the peripheral nervous systems through regulation of neuron survival, proliferation, migration, differentiation, and synapse formation and plasticity. It is a receptor for BDNF/brain-derived neurotrophic factor and NTF4/neurotrophin-4. Alternatively can also bind NTF3/neurotrophin-3 which is less efficient in activating the receptor but regulates neuron survival through NTRK2.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 58 (autosomal dominant); obesity, hyperphagia, and developmental delay (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving NTRK2 have been reported in lung adenocarcinoma, infant-type hemispheric glioma, and NTRK-rearranged spindle cell neoplasm, malignant.
